items.text: A named target in `just ci` scans every `#[test]` and `#[tokio::test]` function in the workspace and reports each one that contains a sleep, an explicit wait or a duration bound.
items.command: grep -q 'wait-lint' justfile && cargo run -q -p internal-lints --bin wait-lint

items.text: The lint fails with a non-zero status, naming the file, the test function and the offending expression, when it finds one, and prints how many test functions it scanned and how many it flagged.
items.command: cargo run -q -p internal-lints --bin wait-lint crates/internal-lints/tests/fixtures/waiting-crate >/tmp/wait-lint-ac2.txt 2>&1; test $? -ne 0 && grep -q 'scanned 4 test functions' /tmp/wait-lint-ac2.txt && grep -q 'flagged 2 test functions' /tmp/wait-lint-ac2.txt && grep -q 'src/lib.rs:' /tmp/wait-lint-ac2.txt

items.text: A fixture test that sleeps for a fixed duration makes the lint fail naming that test function.
items.command: cargo run -q -p internal-lints --bin wait-lint crates/internal-lints/tests/fixtures/waiting-crate 2>&1 | grep -q 'sleeps_for_a_fixed_duration: sleep: std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10))'

items.text: A test that drives a fake clock or a fake provider is not flagged, so the lint reports only wall-clock waits.
The lint runs offline: it needs no model provider, no network, no credential and no deployed service.
